title: Early Valve Replacement vs Surveillance in Moderate Aortic Stenosis: Meta-Analysis of Randomized and Observational Evidence
authors: Ali Majed; Pia Kmeid; Ayah Safa; Hamza Kahwaji; Hashem Safieddine; Georges Ghanem
abstract: BACKGROUND: Moderate aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with excess mortality, and 2 randomized trials have tested early transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). OBJECTIVES: The authors sought to estimate the effects of early TAVR vs clinical surveillance and to compare randomized with observational estimates. METHODS: Six databases and registries were searched through November 3, 2026. Adjusted observational studies were synthesized separately from trials. Certainty was rated with GRADE. RESULTS: Two trials (922 patients; TAVR UNLOAD, n = 178, HF with reduced ejection fraction; PROGRESS, n = 744, 96.4% symptomatic) and 7 cohorts were included. Early TAVR did not detectably change death over approximately 2 years (HR: 1.05; 95% CI: 0.74-1.49; low certainty), with one-fifth of the deaths needed to detect a 20% reduction. Heart failure (HF) hospitalization was lower (RR: 0.53; 95% CI: 0.36-0.77; low certainty), or 70 fewer patients per 1,000 at 2 years. New pacemakers were more frequent (PROGRESS: 17.3% vs 9.3%; moderate certainty). About half of surveillance patients underwent valve replacement within 2 years. Observational cohorts estimated a 48% mortality reduction (HR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.43-0.64; very low certainty), which differed from the randomized estimate (ratio of HRs: 2.01; 95% CI: 1.37-2.95). CONCLUSIONS: In older, predominantly symptomatic patients with moderate AS, early TAVR may make little or no difference to 2-year mortality and may reduce HF hospitalization, at the cost of more pacemakers. Because about half of patients under surveillance receive a valve within 2 years, the decision largely concerns timing. Observational survival estimates should not guide practice.

title: Laparoscopic Transabdominal Preperitoneal (TAPP) Hernioplasty with Overlapping Mesh Technique for Large Direct Inguinal Hernia in an Elderly Patient with Prior Contralateral TEP Repair: A Case Report
authors: Trần Quế Sơn; Mai Van Vuong; Tran Thu Huong; Nguyen Chi Trung; Nong Ngoc Quang
journal: VNU Journal of Science Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences
abstract: Abstract: Background: Managing large direct inguinal hernias in elderly patients with a history of prior transabdominal preperitoneal (TEP) repair on the contralateral side presents a significant surgical challenge due to severe fibrosis and anatomical distortion within the Retzius space. Case Presentation: We report the case of an 86-year-old male presenting with a large left direct inguinal hernia (defect >3 cm) containing small bowel, colon, and omentum. The patient had a previous contralateral TEP hernia repair six years prior. A transabdominal preperitoneal (TAPP) approach was utilized, involving meticulous adhesiolysis of the retro-pubic space followed by the placement of overlapping 10x15 cm polypropylene meshes to reinforce the myopectineal orifice, supplemented by prophylactic preperitoneal drainage. The operative time was 132 minutes, with successful reduction of the hernia sac and preservation of vascular structures. Postoperatively, the patient’s comorbidities-hypertension and type 2 diabetes—were strictly managed. The patient experienced an uneventful recovery with no signs of seroma, hematoma, or surgical site infection, and was discharged on postoperative day 7. Conclusion: TAPP combined with an overlapping mesh technique represents a effective solution for complex, large direct inguinal hernias in elderly patients with a history of prior contralateral preperitoneal surgery. This approach provides an enhanced visualization for navigating distorted anatomical planes and ensures robust abdominal wall reconstruction. Keywords: Direct inguinal hernia, TAPP, TEP, overlapping mesh, elderly.

title: Door-to-Valve Time and Clinical Outcomes in Acute Decompensated Severe Aortic Stenosis: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Jeff  Runqi Ma; Mark Gerges; Anoop Ninan Koshy; WILLIAM M. WILSON; Andrew J. Taylor; William Chan
abstract: Background: Acute decompensated aortic stenosis (ADAS) carries high mortality, but the optimal timing of valve intervention is unknown. Objective: To assess the association between time to valve intervention (transcatheter aortic valve replacement [TAVR] or balloon aortic valvuloplasty [BAV]) and clinical outcomes in ADAS. Methods: Embase, Ovid MEDLINE and CENTRAL were searched to May 15, 2026. Hazard ratios (HRs) for delayed versus earlier intervention were pooled using random-effects models with modified Hartung-Knapp inference. Unadjusted short-term mortality risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using the Mantel-Haenszel method. Results: Eight observational cohort studies (n=6,044) met inclusion criteria: six TAVR (n= 5,986) and two BAV (n=58) studies. Patients were approximately 79 years old, and 63% were male. Early-intervention thresholds ranged from <24-48 hours (BAV) to ?22 days (TAVR) from admission. Delayed intervention was not significantly associated with long-term all-cause mortality (HR 1.52, 95% CI 0.46-5.00; p=0.269; I2=58.2%) or mortality per five-day delay (HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.34-3.43; p=0.530; I2=86.7%). Crude short-term mortality was higher with delayed intervention (RR 4.96, 95% CI 1.17-20.92; p=0.029; I2=0.0%), although this association was not robust to sensitivity analyses. Most studies were at serious risk of bias, with substantial heterogeneity in clinical severity, intervention timing, and treatment modality. Conclusion: Point estimates favour earlier intervention, but current observational data do not establish a mortality benefit for an optimal door-to-valve interval, and existing study designs are biased against early treatment. Prospective and randomized-controlled trials on optimal valve intervention timing following ADAS are needed.

title: Coagulation abnormalities in children with uncorrected congenital cyanotic heart disorders
authors: Hanan Zekri; Doaa Salah Mahmoud; Sarah Ayman; Mohammed Al Komy
abstract: Abstract Background Congenital Cyanotic heart disease (CCHD) is a congenital defect of the heart that reduces the amount of oxygen delivered to the body. Coagulation is the physiological process of maintaining hemostasis in the body. Multiple coagulation and hematological abnormalities have been found in patients with CCHD that can lead to both bleeding tendency or/and thrombosis. Aim To assess the presence of certain hematological and coagulation abnormalities among pediatric patients with CCHD comparing them to normal control and assess for the presence of complications resulting from these abnormalities. Methods This analytical observational case control study included 76 patients (37 cases diagnosed with congenital cyanotic heart disease and 39 healthy control) with age ranged from 6 months to 13 years old who were following up in pediatric cardiology clinic in Cairo University Specialized Pediatric Hospital. Both cases and control were tested for PT, PTT, INR, CBC differential and D-dimer, the results of both groups were compared. Results Children with congenital cyanotic disease had a statistically significant higher values of PT, PTT, INR and D-dimer compared to healthy controls with P value 0.001, 0.004, < 0.001 and < 0.001 respectively. Also, there was a statistically significant increase in the Hb, HCT in cases when compared with the control group with a (p-value < 0.001). There was a statistically significant decrease in the platelet count in cases group versus control group with p = 0.001. Eight patients (22%) showed thrombocytopenia while three patients (8%) showed thrombocytosis. There was a statistically significant longer duration of cyanosis in patients who developed complications versus patients who didn’t develop complications (p value: 0.014). Conclusion Coagulation abnormalities, in the form of prolonged PT, PTT, INR, D –dimer, high hematocrit values and thrombocytopenia, were found in children with cyanotic heart disease compared to healthy individuals. These abnormalities make them more liable for thrombotic or bleeding complications. So, routine screening of coagulation abnormalities is recommended in these patients which may aid in management decisions while awaiting definitive surgeries.

title: Clinical Decision-Making in High-Risk Cross-Platform Redo-TAVI: Pre-Emptive Coronary Wiring and Chimney Stenting
authors: Sasho Stanisavljevikj; Alexander Staudt; Jens Papenefuss; Christian Jacob; Ahmed Saleh Abu Rumman; Hristijan Alagjozovski; Vladyslav Kavalerchyk; Christian D. Etz; Magdalena Sikole; Ivica Bojovski; Marcus-André Deutsch; Davor Vukadinović; Christian Fahje Klopsch
abstract: Background: Redo transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in patients with prior transapical SAPIEN 3 valves carries a significant risk of coronary obstruction. Chimney stenting is an established strategy to maintain coronary perfusion in high-risk valve-in-valve (ViV) procedures. Case Description: An 87-year-old woman presented with NYHA class IV symptoms due to severe restenosis of a 20-mm SAPIEN 3 valve implanted in 2017. Computed tomography revealed stent extension beyond the sinotubular junction, posing a risk of right coronary artery (RCA) occlusion. A transfemoral redo-TAVI using a 23-mm Medtronic Evolut FX+ valve was performed with pre-positioned chimney stenting. During valve deployment, inferior ST-segment elevation occurred, necessitating immediate RCA stenting. A second distal RCA stent addressed residual stenosis. Final angiography confirmed preserved coronary flow and optimal valve function; Discussion: Careful preprocedural evaluation—including CT-based assessment of coronary height, sinus anatomy, and virtual valve modeling—is essential in high-risk ViV or redo-TAVI cases. The chimney technique provides an effective bailout for acute coronary obstruction, while procedural strategies such as commissural alignment and the cusp-overlap technique can optimize procedural and hemodynamic outcomes.; Conclusions: Planned coronary protection using chimney stenting enables safe and effective redo transfemoral TAVI in patients with complex anatomy and prior transapical valve implantation, ensuring hemodynamic success and minimizing complications.

title: Application of endovascular stent graft in ABO-incompatible living donor kidney transplantation: a case report
authors: Liping Guo; Yeqi Nian; Qing Du; Yang Xu; Sen Yang; Jie Zhao; Wenli Song; Gang Feng
abstract: Severe iliac arteriosclerosis is a contraindication for kidney transplantation (KT). This report details a case of a 34-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus and severe iliac arteriosclerosis who underwent ABO-incompatible living donor KT in which the renal graft artery was anastomosed to the self-expandable endovascular covered stent placed in the external iliac artery. The initial anti-blood group anti-A antibody titers were 1:4 and 1:32 for IgG and IgM, respectively. Routine pre-transplant therapy including rituximab 200mg, triple immunosuppressants included tacrolimus (7mg/d, tacrolimus concentration was between 3.8 and 9.2 ng/mL), mycophenolate mofetil (1500mg/d), methylprednisolone (16mg/d). Following one session of double filtration plasmapheresis, anti-blood group antibody titers were reduced 1:4 and 1:8 for IgG and IgM. Two days prior to surgery, patient underwent one session of plasma exchange and antibody titers were IgG 1:4 and IgM 1:8 on the day of KT. Basiliximab was administered for immune induction. The initial routine was performed with conventional end-to-side anastomosis between the renal graft artery and the right external iliac artery. However, pulsation of the transplant renal artery disappeared shortly. Upon opening the anastomosis, thrombosis at the anastomotic site was identified due to plaque embolism from the external iliac artery. Consequently, a self-expandable endovascular covered stent was implanted into the external iliac artery via the right femoral artery under intervention. Because part of the external iliac artery wall was defective, the endovascular stent was partially exposed, used the prosthetic graft for coverage and reinforcement. Finally, the renal allograft artery was anastomosed end-to-side to the stent–prosthetic complex. The anti-blood group antibody titers were 1:2 and 1:4 for IgG and IgM and serum creatinine was 124 μmol/L at 1 month. During the 2 years follow-up, graft function remained satisfactory, the serum creatinine levels were 116, 107, and 113 μmol/L at 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years postoperatively, and no signs of right lower limb ischemia were evident. This study demonstrates that renal graft implanted on the endovascular stent is a feasible therapeutic option for recipients with severe iliac arteriosclerosis.

title: Multi-modal cardiac analysis: Distinguishing cardiac sarcoidosis from arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy through radiomics and ECG features
authors: Francesca Lo Iacono; Uzma A. Chaudhry; Anna Slättman; Ellen Ostenfeld; Henrik Engblom; Maria Elisabetta Mancini; Claus Graff; Arash Mokhtari; Oscar Ö. Braun; Erik Ljungström; Pyotr G. Platonov; Valentina Corino
abstract: Differentiation between cardiac sarcoidosis (CS) and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC) presents a significant diagnostic challenge due to overlapping clinical presentations. This study aims to develop a machine learning model integrating radiomic and electrocardiogram (ECG)-based features to distinguish between these conditions. The study included 41 CS and 16 ARVC patients. Three machine learning models were developed using cardiac magnetic resonance radiomic features, ECG-based features, and their integration. Data underwent a 5-fold nested cross-validation for feature selection and classifier optimization, with the optimal model retrained on a random training subset (70%) and then evaluated on the remaining 30% test set. Semi-supervised LASSO and logistic regression were selected by the cross-validation as the best performing combination and the Gini index determined the optimal final feature set. The radiomic and ECG-based models achieved F1 scores of 0.88 [0.83–0.92] and 0.92 [0.88–0.96], respectively, while the integrated model demonstrated superior performance (F1 score: 0.96 [0.92–1]). Explainability analysis identified the radiomic texture parameter glcm_ClusterShade as the most significant feature, followed by two ECG parameters namely P wave peak time (from P onset) in lead V2 and Q wave area in lead V5. This study demonstrates that integrating radiomic and ECG-based data in machine learning models can enhance CS-ARVC differentiation, potentially improving diagnostic accuracy in clinical practice. However, these findings require confirmation in larger cohorts and further validation before their clinical applicability can be established.

title: AI-integrated multi-omics fusion for precision cardiovascular diagnostics
authors: Shihui Xiao; Dengfeng Gao
abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide, requiring accurate and early diagnostic systems for effective intervention. Traditional prediction approaches relying only on clinical data often fail to capture complex biological interactions underlying disease progression. This study proposes CardioPrecision-BioFusion, an AI-driven framework that combines clinical, genomic, transcriptomic, and simulated proteomic representations. The clinical and omics datasets were obtained from independent cohorts and were not patient matched; consequently, the framework performs cohort-level latent representation integration and does not claim patient-level multi-omics fusion. Modality-specific encoders, target-blind prototype retrieval, multi-head attention, transformer-based learning, an autoencoder, and stacking were used to model heterogeneous feature interactions, while masked attention handled structurally unavailable modalities without imputing unobserved patient-level omics measurements. On the internal held-out constructed fusion test set, the model achieved 97.96% accuracy (95% CI, 97.14–98.55%), 98.05% precision, 98.05% recall, and a 98.05% F1-score. In a source-disjoint, transcriptomics-only external evaluation using 332 samples from GSE141910, the frozen transcriptomics branch achieved 84.64% accuracy and an AUC-ROC of 91.20%. SHAP analysis identified influential clinical and molecular features. These findings support the framework as an exploratory multimodal methodology, but prospective validation in patient-matched multi-omics cohorts is required before clinical use.

title: Reliability and readability of large language model chatbot responses to public-facing questions about hypertension, antihypertensive therapy, and erectile dysfunction: a cross-sectional comparative study
authors: Junke Luo; Shaoyong Chen
abstract: Abstract Background Large language model (LLM) chatbots are increasingly used as public-facing sources of health information. This study compared the reliability, information quality, source transparency, and readability of four publicly accessible LLM chatbots responding to questions about hypertension, antihypertensive therapy, and erectile dysfunction (ED). Methods In this cross-sectional web-based study, 37 questions were retained from a 99-item pool informed by MeSH/PubMed, Google Trends, and recurring themes on publicly accessible Chinese online platforms. On May 22, 2026, each question was submitted once in a new conversation to ChatGPT 5.5, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini 3.5 Flash, and Perplexity, yielding 148 responses. Two blinded clinicians independently rated responses using DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA, and GQS; readability was assessed with six indices. Results Inter-rater agreement was excellent for DISCERN and EQIP (ICC(2,1) = 0.982 and 0.991) and almost perfect for JAMA and GQS (quadratic-weighted kappa = 0.851 and 0.92). Perplexity had the highest median DISCERN (47.00), EQIP (75.00), and JAMA (1.00) scores, with significant between-model differences (all P < 0.001). GQS did not differ significantly (P = 0.055; all medians 4.00). No model met the prespecified sixth-grade readability target; Copilot was descriptively easiest to read, but its median FKGL was 11.65 and FRES 38.60. Conclusion In this single-date benchmark, Perplexity achieved higher structured quality and transparency scores, whereas readability remained poor across all models. The findings support cautious use of general-purpose LLMs as supplementary rather than standalone patient-education sources and highlight the need for clearer source attribution and plain-language optimization.

title: CTHRC1 mitigates dystrophic aortic valve calcification by suppressing foamy macrophage-mediated inflammatory remodeling
authors: Tomohisa Sakaue; Hiroshi Sakamoto; Mika Hamaguchi; Yasuhisa Nakao; Mie Kurata; Akiyasu Iwase; Hiroki Kurihara; Yosuke Kiriyama; Takuma Fukunishi; Kurobe Hirotsugu; Takashi Nishimura; Shunji Uchita; Daisuke Shiokawa; Yoshiaki Kubota; Osamu Yamaguchi; Hironori Izutani
abstract: Abstract Although aortic stenosis (AS) represents a major cardiovascular burden, the molecular mechanisms underlying aortic valve calcification remain unclear. Spatial transcriptomic analysis of injured valve leaflets identified Cthrc1 (collagen triple helix repeat containing 1) as a prominently induced factor within the valvular interstitium. CTHRC1 elevation in expanded valvular interstitial cells (VICs) of thickened murine valve leaflets was validated by immunohistochemistry, and similar CTHRC1 upregulation was confirmed in human stenotic aortic valves. Lineage-tracing analyses demonstrated that the expanded VIC population in thickened murine valve leaflets following wire injury was derived predominantly from PDGFRβ-positive interstitial cells, with little contribution from endothelial cells. Although hemodynamic alterations were comparable between Cthrc1 −/− and wild-type AS mice, Cthrc1 deficiency markedly exacerbated valvular calcification during the chronic phase. Further spatial transcriptomic analyses of Cthrc1 −/− AS mice revealed extensive accumulation of Galectin-3-positive foamy macrophages within the interstitial space of stenotic valves in Cthrc1 −/− mice compared with wild-type controls. Moreover, stenotic valves from Cthrc1 −/− mice exhibited depletion of respiratory-chain signatures and upregulation of cell death–associated pathways, suggesting that CTHRC1, transiently induced during the acute phase following valvular endothelial injury, protects against subsequent dystrophic calcification.

title: Wearable E‐Textiles for Cardiovascular Monitoring: Materials, Devices, and Integrated Systems
authors: Bangul Khan; Mahmoud Tavakoli; Norbert Radacsi; Bee Luan Khoo
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, highlighting the need for continuous, non-invasive, and reliable physiological monitoring beyond conventional clinical assessments. Smart textiles have emerged as a promising platform for personalized cardiovascular healthcare by combining wearability, mechanical comfort, and seamless integration into everyday garments. This review examines recent advances in conductive materials, textile manufacturing technologies, and system-level device integration for cardiovascular sensing applications. Metallic fibers, carbon nanomaterials, and conducting polymers are evaluated for electrical conductivity, stretchability, mechanical durability, and wash stability. Furthermore, textile fabrication approaches, including weaving, knitting, embroidery, printing, and electrospinning, are analyzed for their ability to translate material properties into scalable, manufacturable sensing architectures. Recent developments in textile-integrated electrocardiography, pulse-wave, blood pressure, and hemodynamic monitoring demonstrate performance approaching clinical standards, with high signal fidelity and strong agreement with conventional medical devices. Key challenges related to long-term stability, power autonomy, signal reliability, and large-scale manufacturing are discussed alongside emerging solutions, including MXene-based electrodes, self-powered sensing systems, and edge artificial intelligence. Finally, future perspectives are outlined for developing clinically validated, scalable, and intelligent smart textile platforms that enable continuous cardiovascular monitoring and next-generation personalized healthcare.

title: Disseminated Tuberculosis Complicated by Infectious Aortitis and Pseudoaneurysm in Suspected Takayasu Arteritis
authors: Ana Margarida Morgado; António Padilha; João Marques Cardoso; Joana Lopo; José Ignacio Moreno
abstract: Disseminated tuberculosis with aortic involvement is an uncommon but potentially fatal complication of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection.We report the case of a 25-year-old man from Nepal with a history of renovascular hypertension secondary to renal artery stenosis diagnosed during adolescence, who presented with persistent fever, cough, anorexia, asthenia, and abdominal pain.Microbiologic evaluation confirmed smear-positive pulmonary tuberculosis without rifampicin resistance, and standard first-line antituberculous therapy was initiated.Thoracoabdominopelvic computed tomography demonstrated diffuse reticulonodular pulmonary infiltrates with cavitary lesions, calcified mediastinal lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and extensive aortic calcification.A large periaortic collection immediately inferior to the celiac trunk origin was also identified.Further vascular imaging demonstrated disruption of the vascular wall, critical celiac trunk stenosis, superior mesenteric artery occlusion, and bilateral renal artery occlusion.The combination of early-onset renovascular hypertension and extensive multivessel arterial disease raised suspicion of underlying Takayasu arteritis, while the periaortic lesion was considered consistent with infectious aortitis and pseudoaneurysm formation in the setting of active tuberculosis.The patient declined vascular surgical intervention.He subsequently developed sudden abdominal pain, massive gastrointestinal hemorrhage, severe metabolic acidosis, and refractory shock, followed by cardiac arrest.Autopsy demonstrated disseminated necrotizing granulomatous disease involving the lungs, kidneys, and aortic wall.Histopathologic examination of the aorta revealed transmural arteritis with neutrophilic infiltration, microabscesses, and tissue necrosis, consistent with infectious involvement of the vascular wall and pseudoaneurysm formation.This case highlights the potentially fatal vascular complications of disseminated tuberculosis and the diagnostic complexity of concomitant infectious aortic disease and suspected large-vessel vasculitis.Early recognition of aortic involvement and multidisciplinary assessment are essential in patients presenting with tuberculosis and extensive vascular abnormalities.

title: Multiparametric Extracellular Vesicle Profiling Identifies a Distinct Circulating Signature of Bicuspid Aortic Valve Disease
authors: Luisa Weiß; Amarri Harrison; Sarvesh Chelvanambi; Taku Kasai; Mandy E. Turner; Mark C. Blaser; Marie Billaud; Masanori Aikawa; Sasha A. Singh; Elena Aïkawa
abstract: Background: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) resulting in life-threatening aortic stenosis, heart failure and death, develops earlier and progresses more rapidly in patients with bicuspid aortic valves (BAV) than tricuspid aortic valves (TAV), yet the circulating molecular drivers remain poorly understood. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) capture disease-relevant cellular activation and offer a powerful window into a BAV-specific pathophysiology. Methods: Circulating large extracellular vesicle (LEV) abundance and morphology were characterized by complementary single-vesicle nano-flow cytometry and super-resolution microscopy. Proteomic profiling further delineated LEV molecular cargoes and associated biological pathways between patients with BAV and TAV. Results: We demonstrate that patients with BAVs exhibited fundamentally altered circulating LEV profiles compared to TAVs. Super-resolution imaging revealed BAV-specific organization of platelet- and leukocyte-associated adhesion molecules into discrete EV membrane microdomains. Proteomic profiling identified distinct LEV cargoes between BAV and TAV, including a BAV-specific, previously unrecognized neutrophil-associated signature enriched for proteins involved in neutrophil degranulation and innate immunity. Consistent with this phenotype, BAV displayed alterations in platelet- and neutrophil-associated LEV populations, suggesting enhanced (thrombo-)inflammatory activity. Lastly, distinct associations between LEV populations and clinical parameters in BAV and TAV suggest that LEV profiles reflect morphology-specific aspects of disease severity. Conclusions: Comprehensive single-vesicle analysis and bulk proteomic profiling identified a distinct circulating LEV signature in BAV-associated CAVD, characterized by endothelial activation and reciprocal platelet-neutrophil interactions. These findings reveal previously unrecognized differences in circulating LEVs between BAV and TAV and highlight their potential as biomarkers of valve morphology-specific pathophysiology.

title: Age changes what a risk-factor count tells the referring physician: recorded cardiometabolic burden and obstructive coronary artery disease on CT angiography in a single-centre cross-sectional study
authors: Xiaohua Sun; Huimin Gu; Dongrui Liu
abstract: Abstract Background General practitioners considering coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) usually have only admission diagnoses and recent laboratory results. Whether the number of cardiometabolic risk factors in those records means the same at every age, and whether HbA1c and eGFR add discrimination, is untested. Methods Single-centre cross-sectional study of adult CCTA examinations from the general practice and cardiology pathways of a tertiary hospital, 2021 to 2025. The exposure was the number of hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidaemia and renal impairment recorded from diagnoses and laboratory results within 30 days before CCTA. Obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) was read from reports by a validated text rule. After excluding prior revascularisation and incomplete laboratory data, 5,225 patients were analysed with patient-clustered logistic regression. Results Obstructive CAD was reported in 1,018 patients (19.5%), similarly in both pathways. Each additional risk factor carried an adjusted odds ratio of 1.70 (95% CI 1.57 to 1.84); adjusted prevalence rose from 9.2% with none to 43.9% with four. Age modified the association (interaction P < 0.001): the per-factor odds ratio was 2.20 under 55 years and 1.46 at 75 or older; obstructive CAD without recorded risk factors was 0.4% and 21.2%. Adjusted odds ratios were 4.41 for HbA1c of 8.0% or higher and 1.64 for eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m². Conclusions The recorded risk-factor count shows a dose-response relationship with obstructive CAD that weakens with age. A clean record reassures in younger patients but much less in older ones. HbA1c and eGFR refine risk; risk-factor review before CCTA should be read by age.

title: Platelet-endothelial crosstalk drives distinct endothelial dysfunction in bicuspid aortic valve disease
authors: Luisa Weiß; Sarvesh Chelvanambi; Amarri Harrison; Taku Kasai; Yuto Nakamura; Mandy E. Turner; Mark C. Blaser; Marie Billaud; Masanori Aikawa; Sasha A. Singh; Elena Aïkawa
abstract: Background: Bicuspid aortic valves (BAV) predispose individuals to premature development of aortic stenosis (AS). The abnormal hemodynamic environment of BAV affects both platelets and valvular endothelial cells (VECs), but whether platelet-derived signals contribute to valve morphology-specific endothelial dysfunction remains unknown. Methods: Platelets and VECs were obtained from patients with BAVs or tricuspid aortic valves (TAVs) undergoing valve replacement for AS. Platelets were activated to generate platelet releasate (PR). PR composition and its effects on VECs were investigated using complementary molecular, multi-omic, functional, and computational approaches. Results: BAV and TAV patients exhibited markedly distinct PR profiles, which translated into differential endothelial responses. Strikingly, BAV-derived PR elicited a substantially more pronounced endothelial dysfunction phenotype, characterized by widespread molecular reprogramming and functional alterations. Integrated multi-omics uncovered mitochondrial dysfunction as a central feature of BAV PR-induced endothelial injury, accompanied by activation of pathways spanning endothelial remodeling, migration, and immune-cell recruitment. These molecular signatures translated into mitochondrial depolarization, altered mitochondrial dynamics, enhanced VEC migration, and increased neutrophil adhesion and chemotaxis. Finally, computational ligand-receptor and ligand-target analyses identified candidate signaling axes linking platelet-derived mediators to endothelial reprogramming, highlighting potential therapeutic targets. Conclusions: We provide the first direct evidence that platelet activation contributes to AS initiation through the induction of endothelial dysfunction and that these effects are amplified in BAV. These findings identify platelet-VEC crosstalk as a previously unrecognized mechanism linking abnormal valve hemodynamics to disease onset. Targeting platelet-derived mediators may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for AS, specifically in BAV.

title: Cipepofol combined with esketamine for anesthetic management of patients with extensive severe burns: a retrospective case series
authors: Jinlan Li; Tingting Ni; Xiaodong Lei; Jing Yu; Lili Fang; Wenxiu Ye; Yuanyuan Yao; Min Yan
abstract: Background Patients with extensive severe burns are prone to both hypermetabolic tachycardia and anesthesia-induced hypotension, and their pain is often inadequately controlled with opioids alone. Cipepofol, a novel intravenous hypnotic structurally related to propofol, has shown greater hemodynamic stability than propofol, whereas esketamine provides analgesia and has indirect sympathomimetic activity. We evaluated the feasibility of a cipepofol–esketamine total intravenous anesthesia regimen in this high-risk population. Methods This single-center retrospective case series included consecutive adults with extensive severe burns (total body surface area ≥50% or full-thickness burn ≥20%) undergoing debridement, escharectomy, or skin grafting. Patient characteristics, postoperative complications, and the Day 28/pre-discharge global analgesic assessment were summarized for seven patients. Hemodynamics, bispectral index values, and rescue analgesic use were summarized across 16 procedures, while paired cortisol concentrations were analyzed for 12 procedures. Acute pain data were limited to event-triggered numerical rating scale scores recorded at rescue. Results Seven male patients (mean age, 45.0 ± 11.1 years; mean total body surface area burned, 73.4 ± 17.2%) underwent 16 procedures. Heart rate (HR) was lower after incision. At 90 min, among 10 contributing procedures, the mean within-procedure HR change was −22.8 beats/min (95% CI, −30.4 to −15.1), while the mean arterial pressure (MAP) change was −11.1 mmHg (95% CI, −23.0 to 0.9). Variable sample sizes and wide blood-pressure confidence intervals limited interpretation. Bispectral index values were between 40 and 60 for 65.3 ± 21.0% of valid maintenance time. Rescue analgesia was required after 6/16 procedures, with event-triggered pain scores of 4–6. The late global analgesic rating was excellent or good in all seven patients. Conclusions Cipepofol–esketamine-based multimodal total intravenous anesthesia was feasible in this small series. Prespecified hypotension was common and was managed with intermittent norepinephrine boluses without continuous infusion. The observed arterial pressure profile reflects both the anesthetic regimen and active vasopressor management. With four agents co-administered and no comparator, the contribution of individual agents cannot be isolated. These descriptive findings establish neither comparative safety nor acute analgesic efficacy and require prospective controlled evaluation.

title: Correlation analysis of left atrial appendage morphology and function with ischemic stroke in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation
authors: Shi Peiqing; Yanhan Wang; XU Ding-hu; Chen Jinan; Jiang Ya-bin; Jimeng Yang; Jun Wang
abstract: Abstract Objective: The aim of this study is to analyze the correlations between left atrial appendage (LAA) morphology, LAA function, and other clinical factors with ischemic stroke in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF). Methods: This single-center prospective observational study enrolled consecutive NVAF patients who underwent contrast-enhanced left atrial CT at the Department of Cardiology, Jiangning Hospital Affiliated to Nanjing Medical University from July 2021 to August 2022. Clinical and imaging data were collected at baseline. Survivors were followed annually for a minimum of two years, including repeat cranial CT. Patients were divided into two groups: those without new ischemic stroke during follow-up (Group A) and those with new ischemic stroke (Group B). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was utilized to assess the predictive performance of the CHA2DS2-VASc score alone and in combination with LAA depth and LAA slow blood flow for new ischemic stroke; results are reported as area under the ROC curve (AUC). Results: A total of 100 patients completed the study, with 85 in Group A and 15 in Group B. Group B had significantly higher CHA2DS2-VASc scores, prevalence of hypertension history, statin use, LAA depth, left superior pulmonary vein long diameter, left superior pulmonary vein short diameter, incidence of left atrial thrombus, and LAA slow blood flow (all P < 0.05). Multivariable logistic regression identified hypertension history (OR = 1.092; 95% CI, 1.003–1.188; P = 0.042), LAA depth (OR = 27.923; 95% CI, 1.807–431.513; P = 0.017), and LAA slow blood flow (OR = 5.917; 95% CI, 1.349–25.952; P = 0.018) as independent risk factors for ischemic stroke during follow-up. The AUCs for predicting new ischemic stroke were 0.713 for the CHA2DS2-VASc score alone and 0.825 for the CHA2DS2-VASc score combined with LAA depth and LAA slow blood flow. Conclusion: In patients with NVAF, the risk of ischemic stroke is significant. Furthermore, integrating LAA depth and LAA slow-flow parameters with the CHA2DS2-VASc score substantially enhances its predictive ability for stroke compared to the CHA2DS2-VASc score alone.

title: Device-detected new-onset atrial fibrillation after dual-chamber pacemaker implantation in patients with sick sinus syndrome under managed ventricular pacing: a risk nomogram from the 3-month landmark
authors: Jin-Mei Xie; Cheng-Hua Shan; Ying-Jun Xiao; Jie Ma; Ren-Rong Lü; Zong-Jie Zheng
abstract: Background New-onset atrial fibrillation ( N OAF) is common after dual-chamber pacemaker implantation, but existing prediction models were derived from mixed populations of patients with sick sinus syndrome (SSS) and atrioventricular block and included heterogeneous pacing strategies. Methods In this single-centre retrospective cohort study, consecutive patients with SSS who received a first permanent Medtronic dual-chamber pacemaker with managed ventricular pacing (MVP) enabled as the default strategy were screened. Patients with atrial fibrillation or an atrial high-rate episode (AHRE) within 3 months after implantation were excluded, and prediction time started at this 3-month landmark, with atrial pacing percentage (AP%) and ventricular pacing percentage (VP%) measured at that visit. Patients implanted in 2015–2021 formed the development cohort ( n = 322), and those implanted in 2022–2025 formed a temporal validation cohort ( n = 121) reserved exclusively for validation. Twenty-six candidate predictors were assessed by univariable and multivariable Cox regression with backward Akaike information criterion (AIC) selection. Internal validation repeated the complete model-building procedure within 2,000 bootstrap samples. Temporal performance was assessed using discrimination and calibration at 1, 2 and 3 years after the landmark. Results NOAF occurred in 90 of 322 development patients (28.0%) during a median follow-up of 41.6 months [interquartile range (IQR), 13.7–80.1], and in 28 of 121 temporal validation patients (23.1%) during a median follow-up of 30.5 months (IQR, 8.8–45.9). Age (hazard ratio [HR] per year, 1.043; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.019–1.067), maximum P-wave duration (Pmax; HR per 10 ms, 1.200; 95% CI, 1.085–1.326), left atrial volume index (LAVi; HR per 1 mL/m2, 1.051; 95% CI, 1.030–1.073), AP% > 50% (HR, 1.845; 95% CI, 1.198–2.840) and VP% > 40% (HR, 1.898; 95% CI, 1.045–3.446) were independently associated with NOAF. The apparent C-index was 0.735; repeating the complete model-building procedure within 2,000 bootstrap samples gave a mean optimism of 0.036 and an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.6992. In temporal validation the C-index was 0.769 (95% CI, 0.639–0.873) and cumulative/dynamic AUC values were 0.753, 0.881 and 0.916 at 1, 2 and 3 years after the landmark. Calibration-in-the-large was −0.17, 0.24 and 0.35 and calibration slopes were 0.90, 0.99 and 0.98 at 1, 2 and 3 years, respectively. The 1-year calibration estimate remained least precise, with only five NOAF events by 1 year in the validation cohort. Conclusion In patients with SSS who remained free of atrial arrhythmia through the 3-month post-implantation landmark, a five-variable landmark model showed moderate optimism-corrected discrimination in the development cohort and promising same-centre temporal validation performance, particularly at 2 and 3 years after the landmark. The limited number of validation events, particularly at 1 year, warrants cautious interpretation. Prospective multicentre external validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Interpretable machine learning for postoperative atrial fibrillation after noncardiac surgery
authors: Shuyi Zhu; Yigao Gao; Lin Li; Pingping Wang; Chaowei Zhang; Yunpeng Li; YingWei Chen
abstract: Abstract Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is an important complication after non-cardiac surgery and is associated with adverse short- and long-term outcomes. Accurate perioperative risk stratification remains challenging because POAF risk reflects both baseline atrial substrate and dynamic perioperative physiologic stress. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the INSPIRE perioperative database to develop interpretable prediction models for clinically documented postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) after non-cardiac surgery. POAF was defined as new-onset AF captured during the index hospitalization by electrocardiography or rhythm-monitoring documentation; because a uniform cohort-wide measure of monitoring intensity was not available, the endpoint was interpreted as clinically detected POAF. Candidate predictors were grouped by acquisition window into preoperative, intraoperative, and early postoperative (≤ 24 h) variables to support dynamic perioperative risk assessment rather than a purely preoperative screen. Feature selection was performed with Boruta, model explanation with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and classifier comparison with LASSO logistic regression, AdaBoost, LightGBM, XGBoost, and CatBoost. Because POAF was uncommon, performance was evaluated with AUROC, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, and F1 score after stratified splitting and threshold evaluation; synthetic resampling was not used in the primary analysis. Among 99,887 patients, 1,058 (1.1%) developed clinically documented POAF. Compared with controls, POAF cases were older (median 70 vs. 55 years) and showed substantially greater burdens of hypotension and hypoxemia, including more frequent and prolonged MAP < 65 mmHg and SpO₂ <90%. Boruta retained average diastolic blood pressure, average heart rate, and left atrial enlargement as informative features. SHAP identified valvular disease, surgical duration, cardiopulmonary instability, and related early postoperative events as major contributors, consistent with a dynamic perioperative risk model. Discrimination was good across classifiers, with AUCs ranging from 0.80 to 0.85. AdaBoost and CatBoost achieved the best overall performance (both AUC 0.85), while CatBoost showed higher specificity and PPV. In a large non-cardiac surgical cohort, clinically documented POAF was associated with both baseline atrial substrate and perioperative cardiopulmonary stress. Interpretable ML models, particularly boosting-based methods, showed good discrimination and may support dynamic perioperative risk updating and targeted postoperative surveillance, although monitoring heterogeneity, class imbalance, calibration, and external validation remain important considerations.

title: Frailty management in patients with heart valve disease: a scoping review
authors: Wenhui Yuan; HAN Qiong; Peihuang Dong; Xinglin Zheng; Yuan Chen; Linjing Wu
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify, evaluate, and summarise evidence on frailty management in patients with valvular heart disease to inform the development of frailty management programs for clinical practice. Methods This study adheres to the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) framework and is reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines to guarantee methodological strictness and transparency. The system searched multiple databases and websites to gather evidence on the management of frailty in patients with heart valve disease. The search covered the period from the database's inception to October 2026. Literature screening, quality assessment, evidence extraction, and synthesis were conducted independently by two researchers, and the evidence was graded using the JBI Evidence Grading System (2014 edition). Results After a rigorous literature screening process, a total of 28 publications were included, comprising 3 clinical guidelines, 12 expert consensus documents, 1 systematic review, 1 evidence summary, 6 observational studies, 4 randomised controlled trials, and 1 quasi-experimental study. Through a systematic synthesis of the included literature, a total of 46 pieces of evidence were ultimately compiled, covering five areas: identification and screening assessment of the risk of frailty, comprehensive management, exercise rehabilitation management, multidimensional support management, and continuity of rehabilitation care. Conclusion The 46 pieces of evidence summarised in this study can serve as an evidence-based reference for clinical healthcare professionals when developing frailty management programs; however, as this evidence has not yet been systematically implemented in clinical practice, its effectiveness continues to be further validated by future research. Systematic Review Registration http://ebn.nursing.fudan.edu.cn/home , identifier ES20259514.

title: Development and external validation of a nomogram incorporating the TyG index and prognostic nutritional index for predicting cardiovascular events in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and chronic kidney disease
authors: Feng Wang; Chuanpeng Wang; Ruihao Jiang; Jinguo Cheng; Nianzhao Chen; Liting Zhu
abstract: Background Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) frequently coexists with chronic kidney disease (CKD), representing a high-risk cardiorenal phenotype within the cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) syndrome. Despite the high burden of adverse cardiovascular events in this population, dedicated risk prediction tools remain limited. We aimed to develop and validate a prediction model for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined in this study as the composite of all-cause death and first hospitalization for worsening heart failure, in patients with HFpEF and CKD by integrating biomarkers reflecting metabolic and nutritional-inflammatory status. Methods This retrospective cohort study included a development cohort of 2,363 consecutive patients with HFpEF and CKD between January 2012 and December 2023. The development cohort was randomly divided into a training cohort (70%) and an internal validation cohort (30%). An independent cohort of 713 patients from Wenzhou TCM Hospital of Zhejiang Chinese Medical University was used for external validation. Predictor selection was performed using Cox proportional hazards regression, and a nomogram was constructed based on the final multivariable model. Model performance was evaluated using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots, decision curve analysis, and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Results During a median follow-up of 1.41 years, 1,085 patients (45.9%) experienced MACE. The final multivariable model retained age, atrial fibrillation, ACEI/ARB/ARNI therapy, serum creatinine, mean E/e’, pulmonary arterial systolic pressure, triglyceride–glucose (TyG) index, and prognostic nutritional index (PNI). The nomogram showed good discrimination in the training cohort (AUC 0.764, 0.825, and 0.813 for predicting 1-, 3-, and 5-year MACE, respectively) and in the internal validation cohort (AUC 0.724, 0.757, and 0.868). Calibration analysis demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and decision curve analysis indicated favorable clinical utility. The SHAP analysis highlighted key predictors. Benchmark comparison with the MAGGIC score showed higher time-dependent AUCs for the proposed model in the internal validation cohort. In the independent external validation cohort, the 1-, 3-, and 5-year AUC values were 0.800, 0.804, and 0.831, respectively. Calibration and decision curve analyses demonstrated generally acceptable agreement and clinically relevant net benefit. Conclusion A nomogram incorporating the TyG index and prognostic nutritional index demonstrated promising predictive performance for MACE in patients with HFpEF and CKD. These markers may provide complementary prognostic information beyond conventional clinical predictors. Further prospective, multicenter, and geographically diverse validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Oral anticoagulants and the risk of acute kidney injury: a retrospective real-world cohort study using overlap propensity score weighting
authors: Ping Li; Tian Fang-yuan; Hao-Bo Liu; Man Rao; Wenjun Yin; Xiao-cong Zuo; Lingyun Zhou
abstract: Background Anticoagulant-related nephropathy, initially described in association with warfarin, has increasingly been reported with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). However, the comparative risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) within 30 days of treatment initiation between warfarin and DOACs across a broad spectrum of clinical indications remains unclear. Methods This retrospective cohort study included patients newly initiated on DOACs or warfarin between January 2014 and May 2025 at the Third Xiangya Hospital of Central South University. Overlap propensity score weighting, with weights derived from a generalized boosted model incorporating 81 baseline covariates, balanced the treatment groups. Weighted logistic regression compared the risk of AKI within 30 days of OAC initiation, defined by KDIGO criteria. Sensitivity analyses included inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and logistic regression-derived overlap weighting, each with or without doubly robust covariate adjustment. Results Among 6 876 patients (5 048 DOAC users; 1 828 warfarin users), DOAC initiation was associated with a higher risk of AKI than warfarin after overlap weighting (OR: 1.346, 95% CI: 1.057–1.715; p = 0.016), and with severe AKI (stage 2–3; OR: 1.694, 95% CI: 1.013–2.832; p = 0.044), whereas stage 1 AKI did not differ significantly. The association persisted after additional covariate adjustment (OR: 1.363, 95% CI: 1.068–1.740; p = 0.013) and across alternative propensity score models, although the unadjusted IPTW model did not. By indication, the association was significant for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF) (OR: 1.566, 95% CI: 1.034–2.369; p = 0.034) but not for venous thromboembolism (VTE) treatment or prophylaxis. Among individual DOACs, rivaroxaban was associated with an elevated risk (OR: 1.392, 95% CI: 1.075–1.804; p = 0.012), whereas edoxaban, dabigatran, and apixaban were not. Lower-dose rivaroxaban initiation was associated with an increased risk (OR: 2.792, 95% CI: 1.524–5.114; p = 0.001), whereas higher-dose and off-label use were not. In prespecified subgroup analyses, ORs were above 1 in most strata, but most comparisons were not significant, and no significant interactions were detected. Conclusion These findings suggest that DOACs, particularly rivaroxaban, may be associated with a higher short-term risk of AKI than warfarin. Given the expanding use of DOACs, medication-specific renal effects warrant further investigation, and close monitoring of renal function may be advisable in high-risk patients after anticoagulation initiation.

title: Living with an Open-Ended Risk of Stroke: A Qualitative Study of Adults Identified as Being at High Risk of Stroke Without Prior Stroke or TIA in China
authors: Ning Ding; Shiyi Wu; Binghu Li; Qiuyue Huang; Jiaxin Gan; Jie Jing; Xiaochen Ma
abstract: Abstract Background Stroke screening can identify adults without previous stroke or transient ischaemic attack (TIA) as being at high risk and bring them into preventive care. Yet little is known about how people without a cerebrovascular event interpret and live with this risk status. Guided by the “patients-in-waiting” concept, this study explored how adults at high risk of stroke understood their risk classification, integrated risk management into everyday life, and sustained prevention over time. Methods This qualitative descriptive study, informed by naturalistic inquiry, used individual semi-structured interviews. Using maximum-variation purposive sampling, we recruited 21 adults without previous stroke or TIA from two community health centres in Chengdu, China. Interviews conducted from May to June 2026 were analyzed using theory-informed thematic analysis guided by Braun and Clarke’s six-phase framework. The “patients-in-waiting” concept informed interpretation while the analysis remained open to findings beyond the concept. Results Three themes were identified. Making sense of being at high risk showed that participants accepted, distanced themselves from, or recalibrated the classification according to bodily experience, family history, perceived control, and uncertainty about future stroke. Fitting risk management into everyday life showed that participants incorporated manageable practices into routines, negotiated recommendations against enjoyment, relationships, work, and personal priorities, and sometimes made prevention a shared family practice. Maintaining direction in ongoing risk management showed that sustaining prevention depended on accessible care, actionable guidance, usable information, and follow-up feedback that helped participants interpret changes in modifiable risk factors and health indicators over time. Conclusions High-risk classification did not automatically produce a stable patient identity. Instead, participants lived with an open-ended and negotiated risk state in which future stroke remained uncertain and prevention had to be continually interpreted and fitted into everyday life. Primary stroke prevention should extend beyond risk identification by providing accessible, tailored, actionable, and sustained follow-up support.

title: Frailty assessment and individualized exercise prescription in cardiac rehabilitation: current evidence and future directions
authors: Manmeet Kaur Bhalla
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Frailty is an increasingly important clinical consideration in cardiac rehabilitation (CR), particularly among older adults and patients with heart failure, coronary artery disease, valvular disorders, and multiple chronic conditions. It is characterized by reduced physiological reserve and increased vulnerability to adverse outcomes following relatively minor physical or psychological stressors. Frail cardiac patients may experience muscle weakness, slow gait, impaired balance, fatigue, reduced exercise tolerance, nutritional deficiencies, cognitive difficulties, and limitations in activities of daily living. These factors can affect rehabilitation participation, exercise tolerance, adherence, and long-term functional recovery. Traditional cardiac rehabilitation programmes have primarily emphasized aerobic conditioning, cardiovascular risk-factor management, and general exercise capacity. However, these approaches may not adequately address the multidimensional impairments associated with frailty. Contemporary rehabilitation therefore requires systematic frailty screening, comprehensive functional assessment, and individualized exercise prescription based on the patient's dominant limitations, clinical stability, comorbidities, and personal goals. Validated instruments such as the Fried Frailty Phenotype, Clinical Frailty Scale, Edmonton Frail Scale, FRAIL questionnaire, Frailty Index, and Short Physical Performance Battery can support identification and monitoring of frailty. Exercise interventions for frail cardiac patients should generally combine progressive resistance training, aerobic conditioning, balance activities, functional mobility exercises, and flexibility training, with nutritional and psychosocial support when indicated. Evidence from the REHAB-HF trial and recent systematic reviews suggests that multidomain rehabilitation can improve physical function and frailty-related outcomes in selected patients with cardiovascular disease. A 2024 systematic review found that frailty is common among CR participants and that frailty status can improve following programme participation, although considerable variation exists in assessment tools and intervention design. More recent European guidance explicitly recommends offering CR to eligible patients with frailty rather than withholding rehabilitation because of frailty or comorbidities. This review examines the concepts and mechanisms of frailty, clinical assessment methods, and evidence for exercise-based interventions, individualized prescription strategies, safety considerations, multidisciplinary care, implementation barriers, and future research priorities. It proposes a practical framework for integrating frailty assessment into routine cardiac rehabilitation and translating assessment findings into progressive, patient-centred exercise programmes.

title: Lifestyle risk indicators and health promotion priorities among adults with heart failure in Hargeisa Somaliland: a hospital based cross sectional study
authors: Abdirahman Ali Osman; Vitalis Okath; Abdikarim Mousse Duale; Ahmed Mousse Ahmed
abstract: Background Evidence on lifestyle-related health-promotion needs among people receiving heart- failure care in Somaliland is scarce. This study estimated the prevalence of self-reported cigarette smoking, lack of regular physical activity, and self-rated dietary patterns among adults with heart failure attending a specialist cardiac center in Hargeisa. Methods A hospital-based cross-sectional survey was conducted in March 2026 among 200 adults with a clinical diagnosis of heart failure who were recruited at Indo Gargaar Metro Cardiac Center. A structured, interviewer-administered questionnaire assessed self-reported cigarette smoking, regular physical activity, and self-rated diet. Categorical data were summarized using frequencies, percentages, and 95% Wilson confidence intervals (CIs). The analysis was descriptive because all participants had heart failure and no comparison group or longitudinal outcome was available. Results Of the 200 participants, 149 (74.5%) were men, 98 (49.0%) were aged 60 years or older, and 148 (74.0%) lived in urban areas. Self-reported cigarette smoking was reported by 90 participants (45.0%; 95% CI: 38.3–51.9), while 117 reported no regular physical activity (58.5%; 95% CI: 51.6–65.1). Nine participants (4.5%) rated their diet as healthy, 147 (73.5%) as moderate, and 44 (22.0%) as unhealthy. Overall, 191 (95.5%; 95% CI: 91.7–97.7) did not rate their diet as healthy. Conclusion Self-reported cigarette smoking, reported inactivity, and perceived suboptimal diet were common in this clinic-based sample. Heart-failure services should incorporate standardized lifestyle screening, individualized education, and culturally appropriate smoking-cessation, activity, and nutrition support. These findings describe patients receiving specialist care and should not be interpreted as population prevalence or as evidence that the measured behaviors caused heart failure.

title: Prognostic value of model for end-stage liver disease excluding international normalized ratio score combined with late gadolinium enhancement in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
authors: Linsong Leng; Shuai Zhang; Tianhao Wei; Dachuan Guo; Qian Wang; Yu Bai; Sha Chen; Chenxi Zhao; Huixia Lu; Cheng Zhang; Jianmin Yang
abstract: Introduction Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is one of the main subtypes of heart failure (HF). Model for end-stage liver disease excluding international normalized ratio (MELD-XI) score and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) each independently predict adverse prognosis in HF patients. Methods This retrospective study enrolled adult HFrEF patients admitted to Qilu Hospital of Shandong University between September 2018 and January 2023. The primary endpoint was defined as a composite endpoint of rehospitalization for HF and all-cause mortality. Multivariate Cox regression model was established to evaluate the effects of LGE and MELD-XI score on the primary endpoint. We also evaluate the incremental prognostic value of adding the MELD-XI score to the model. Results A total of 246 HFrEF patients were included and 55 patients reached the primary endpoint during follow-up. In the adjusted Cox regression model, for each standard deviation increase in LGE and MELD-XI score, the hazard ratios (HRs) for primary endpoint were 1.52 (95% CI: 1.23–1.88) and 1.60 (95% CI: 1.31–1.94), respectively. Adding MELD-XI score into model improved its incremental prognostic performance [ Δ C-Statistic: 0.052 (95% CI: 0.001–0.092), p = 0.039; Continuous NRI: 0.399 (95% CI: 0.077–0.532), p = 0.027; IDI: 0.094 (95% CI: 0.018–0.174), p = 0.010]. Conclusions Both CMR-assessed LGE and MELD-XI score were associated with adverse outcomes in patients with HFrEF. Combining these two indicators provided complementary prognostic information for HFrEF patients.

title: NLRP3 inflammasome-driven inflammation as a cause of atrial fibrillation: potential synergistic inhibition of the NLRP3 via upstream magnesium repletion and targeting NLRP3 with a downstream inhibitor
authors: Alan A. Wanderer
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most prevalent sustained cardiac arrhythmia. Current therapeutic approaches (antiarrhythmic/rate control medications, anticoagulation, cardioversion, catheter ablation, and cardiac surgery) are effective in selected patients but are associated with adverse effects and significant recurrence rates. These limitations underscore the need for novel adjunctive therapeutic strategies. Substantial biomarker and histopathologic evidence demonstrates chronic inflammation in AF; however, the mechanisms that initiate and sustain this process remain incompletely defined. Emerging evidence suggests that cytokine-driven innate immune activation, rather than adaptive autoimmune mechanisms, is involved, supporting the concept that AF represents a previously unrecognized autoinflammatory disorder. The most widely studied inflammasome protein in AF is NLRP3, a central regulator of innate immunity and a key mechanism controlling the release of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18 that can initiate influx of inflammatory cells causing unchecked inflammation and end-stage fibrosis. Intracellular calcium (Ca 2 +) can stimulate the NLRP3 inflammasome, which can be inhibited upstream by elemental magnesium (Mg 2+ ). The hypothesis proposes that AF is, in part, a dysregulated autoinflammatory condition driven by persistent activation of NLRP3 inflammasome (NLRP3) from endogenous danger-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) derived from common cardiometabolic conditions, such as obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, along with AF triggers, especially excessive alcohol and tobacco consumption. Furthermore, NLRP3-mediated inflammation, combined with Mg 2+ deficiency, may contribute to an energy deficit in sinoatrial (SA) node cardiomyocytes, thereby impairing the electrical automaticity that generates sinus rhythm (SR). Lastly, it is hypothesized reduced AF burden may occur by a synergistic therapeutic strategy combining pharmacokinetic-based oral Mg 2+ supplementation with downstream inhibitors of NLRP3. Reports in the medical literature indicating inconsistent clinical efficacy of oral Mg 2+ controlling AF may reflect underappreciation of Mg 2+ pharmacokinetics involving slow intracellular repletion, and suboptimal Mg 2+ formulations. Addressing these factors may bridge the translational gap and enable standardized oral Mg 2+ based adjunctive therapy for AF.

title: Perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy in resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a phase 2 trial
authors: Xiaoliang Zhao; Bin Zhang; Chenguang Li; Lianmin Zhang; Meng Wang; Ziqiang Tian; Shengguang Wang; Qiang Zhang; Huilai Lv; Chong Pang; Shiwang Wen; Xiaofei Wang; Wei Wei; Yu Zhang; Huang Wuhao; Jianquan Zhu; Yue Li; Chen Chen; Yao Tang; Bin Jia; Hua Zhang; Hui Chen; Sha Wang; Jun-Ye Zhang; Wenting Li; Zhongmin Maxwell Wang; Boning Li; Michelle Xia; Zhenfa Zhang; Dongsheng Yue; Changli Wang
abstract: Resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) carries a high risk of postoperative recurrence, underscoring the need for effective perioperative therapies. This nonrandomized, noncomparative phase 2 trial evaluated neoadjuvant ivonescimab monotherapy (cohort 1) or in combination with chemotherapy (cohort 2), followed by surgery and adjuvant ivonescimab. In cohort 2, the major pathological response (MPR) rate was 70.1% (47/67; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 57.7-80.7); the lower bound of the 80% two-sided CI exceeded the historical control rate of 41% and the primary endpoint was met. The MPR rate in cohort 1 was 60.0% (6/10; 95% CI = 26.2-87.8). Among patients who achieved MPR, 83.3% (5/6) in cohort 1 and 97.9% (46/47) in cohort 2 had residual viable tumor (RVT) of ≤5%, respectively. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events (AEs) occurred in 36.4% (4/11) patients in cohort 1 and 30.4% (24/79) of those in cohort 2, with no grade 3 or higher hemorrhage or treatment-related death. Treatment-related surgery delay occurred in one (1.3%) patient. Surgery-related AEs related to ivonescimab occurred in 10.0% (1/10) and 10.4% (7/67) patients in the two cohorts, respectively, with no grade 3 or higher events reported. These data support perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy as a promising strategy for resectable NSCLC. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05247684 .

title: Structure-specific variation in pediatric echocardiographic Z scores across the nutritional spectrum: four body-surface-area nomograms and a BMI-adjusted GAMLSS model
authors: Rodolfo Amstein; Valentina Metcalfe; Claudia Trincado G.; Álvaro Passi‐Solar; Guillermo Larios G.
abstract: Abstract Purpose Z score nomograms, the standard for interpreting pediatric echocardiographic dimensions, derive mostly from eutrophic populations. We assessed whether cardiac structure Z scores vary with body mass index Z score (BMIz) across four body-surface-area (BSA)-based nomograms, and whether a BMI-adjusted reference mitigates this bias. Methods Retrospective study of 1883 children aged 5–18 years with structurally normal echocardiograms (2016–2021). Eleven cardiac structure diameters were analyzed and Z scores computed with four nomograms (Pediatric Heart Network, Detroit, Toronto, Italy) and, for ten structures, with a fifth based on generalized additive models for location, scale and shape (GAMLSS) adjusted for body size, BMI and age. Associations with BMIz used linear regression in three nested models with false discovery rate correction. Results Overall, 25.8% were overweight and 15.8% had obesity. Absolute diameters increased with BMIz in every structure (p < 0.001), yet Z scores of most left-sided structures were inversely associated with it, most strongly for the four aortic levels (β − 0.325 to − 0.182, significant in all 45 nomogram-by-model comparisons) and for left ventricular end-diastolic diameter. Ventricular walls showed no consistent pattern; right-sided annuli varied non-monotonically. Under GAMLSS these associations were abolished in the most affected structures, persisted in the sinotubular junction and walls, and reversed in sign in the pulmonary annulus. Conclusion Z scores of most left-sided structures were lower in obesity than their absolute dimensions suggest, so interpretation must account for nutritional status and the reference. Persisting bias follows model construction: the three structures whose GAMLSS equations omit BMI are exactly those still biased.

title: Impact of Anti-drug Antibodies in Patients with Fabry Disease under Enzyme Replacement Therapy: Long-Term Outcomes
authors: Malte Lenders; Elisa Rudolph; Robert Radke; Peter Nordbeck; Eva Brand
abstract: Neutralizing anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) against enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) in Fabry disease (FD) are associated with disease progression despite therapy in affected male patients. The aim of this study was to assess the long-term effects of ADAs on clinical outcomes. We analyzed the long-term outcomes of ADA-positive ( n = 24) and ADA-negative ( n = 28) male patients under agalsidase alfa or beta. The assessment included Fabry-associated clinical events (FACEs), determination of cardiac and renal function, evaluation of FD-related symptoms, and the analysis of plasma globotriaosylsphingosine (lyso-Gb 3 ) values. Median observation time was 10 years. ADA-positive and ADA-negative patients presented with comparable disease burden at baseline. Although there were no significant differences in the overall event rate of FACEs ( p = 0.114), ADA-positive patients had an increased risk of ischemic cardiac events, an increase in interventricular septum thickness in diastole (median difference 0.25 mm per year; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.06–0.42; p = 0.0053), and a steeper decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (median difference −0.39 ml/min/1.73 m 2 per year; 95% CI −2.40 to 0.25; p = 0.0554). Macroalbuminuria and high-risk patients according to Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guidelines at baseline resulted in an accelerated yearly eGFR decline of −6.5 in ADA-positive patients ( p < 0.001) versus −2.1 ml/min/1.73 m 2 in ADA-negative patients ( p = 0.0177; comparison: p = 0.0079). The lyso-Gb 3 decrease was more pronounced in ADA-negative patients ( p = 0.0407). Compared to ADA-negative patients, ADA-positive male patients with FD show significantly worse clinical long-term outcomes under ERT. They should be classified as high-risk patients, undergo close monitoring, and receive intensive treatment. Immune tolerance induction to prevent ADAs might be considered to improve the therapeutic efficacy in future.
